memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, do not go into their house to get what is offered to you as a pledge. Stay outside and let the neighbor to whom you are making the loan bring the pledge out to you. - Deut 24:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is another law of remarkable sensitivity. When lending to a neighbour, the lender was not to barge into the borrower's home to seize the pledge for the loan. Instead, he was to wait outside and let the borrower bring it out to him. Even a person in debt was to be treated with dignity, their home respected, their privacy honoured. Being in need did not make someone fair game for humiliation.

Think about the kindness woven into this command. A person borrowing out of poverty was already in a vulnerable position. God would not allow that vulnerability to be exploited or their dignity trampled. The lender had rights, but those rights did not include invading and shaming the borrower. God protects the honour of the poor.

This reflects God's deep concern for treating all people, especially the struggling, with respect and dignity. It is easy to look down on those who owe us something, or to feel entitled to treat them however we wish. But God calls His people to honour the dignity of everyone, regardless of their circumstances. Jesus consistently treated the poor and lowly with tenderness and respect, never with contempt. We are called to do the same, showing kindness and preserving the dignity of those who are struggling. How can you treat those in difficult circumstances with the dignity God says they deserve?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat struggling people with dignity and respect?
2. Where are you tempted to look down on those in need?
3. How does Jesus' treatment of the lowly guide you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me honour the dignity of everyone, especially those who are struggling. Teach me to show the tender respect that Jesus showed. Amen.
